δεκεμβρίων ἀπεστάλησαν. Κυρίοις τιμιωτάτοις καὶ ἁγιωτάτοις ἀδελφοῖς καὶ
συνεπισκόποις Αὐρηλίῳ, Βαλεντίνῳ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ ἐν Καρχηδόνι συναθροισθείσῃ
ἁγιωτά 423 τῃ συνόδῳ, Κύριλλος ἀσπαζόμενος ἐν κυρίῳ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀγάπην. Τὰ
γραφέντα παρὰ τῆς ὑμετέρας τιμιότητος πολλὴν ἔχοντα θρησκείαν μετὰ πάσης
χαρᾶς διὰ τοῦ τέκνου ἡμῶν Ἰννοκεντίου τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου ἐδεξάμην.
Τούτων δὲ παρ' ἡμῶν ἐλπισθέντων, ὥστε ἐκ τοῦ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἐκκλησίας
pass_a_gloss: Tail of the date line: the December kalends fix the dispatch day. Cyril’s formal address to his lords and brothers Aurelius and Valentinus and every bishop met at Carthage, joined with a greeting in the Lord to their loving fellowship. His warm welcome of their devout letter, delivered by Innocent the priest, whom he calls his son. The request restated as a hope laid on Alexandria: that the church archive there would furnish the synod with its most trustworthy transcript of the genuine Nicene meeting in Bithynia’s chief city.
pass_b_english: of December they were sent. To my most honored and most holy lords, brothers and fellow bishops Aurelius and Valentinus, and to the whole most holy synod gathered at Carthage — Cyril, greeting your charity in the Lord.
What your honor wrote, full of deep devotion, I received with all joy through our son Innocent the presbyter.
And since you set this hope upon us — that from the archive of our church we would send to your charity the truest copies of the authentic synod held in Nicaea, the metropolis of Bithynia,

choices.choice: Your charity: standard epistolary address for the recipients’ fellowship.
Archive: Latin scrinium, the church’s record chest.
Opens lowercase finishing the date; closes without a period into rem-mid.
